title: 2 Thessalonians
summary: 2 Thessalonians is a biblical book focused on endurance, judgment, and correction about the day of the Lord.
historical_context: Second Thessalonians comforts a pressured church and corrects confusion about Christ's return.
ancient_near_east_context: 2 Thessalonians belongs to the ancient Mediterranean and Near Eastern world reflected in its setting, institutions, and canonical placement.
hebraic_worldview: 2 Thessalonians should be read with attention to covenant memory, communal identity, worship, wisdom, and accountability before the Lord.
second_temple_context: Second Temple readers received 2 Thessalonians as part of Israel's Scriptures and read it within questions of identity, worship, exile, and hope.
canonical_context: Within Pauline Epistles, book 9 of 13, 2 Thessalonians contributes to the Bible's unfolding witness by connecting endurance, judgment, and correction about the day of the Lord to the larger storyline.
later_christian_reception: Christian interpretation has read 2 Thessalonians as part of the canonical witness to faithfulness, judgment, mercy, and hope in Christ-centered Scripture reading.
literary_context: 2 Thessalonians uses epistle within Pauline Epistles, book 9 of 13 to develop its themes through the book's structure and key passages.
covenantal_significance: 2 Thessalonians helps readers trace covenant faithfulness, failure, mercy, and hope within its canonical setting.
authorship_positions: Traditional Pauline authorship or Pauline circle attribution
Critical scholarship debates several letters and recognizes co-workers in some correspondence
date_ranges: Some disputed letters are placed later or in the Pauline school
original_audience: Mixed Jewish-Gentile congregations and church leaders across the Roman world
historical_setting: The Greco-Roman world of mission, patronage, and local house churches
canonical_role: 2 Thessalonians anchors endurance, judgment, and correction about the day of the Lord within Pauline Epistles, book 9 of 13 and connects the book to related people, places, events, and themes.
structure: Clarification about the day of the Lord
interpretive_disputes: How doctrine, ethics, and pastoral counsel fit together

related_objects.notes: Paul frames the letter's pastoral correction and encouragement.
The Thessalonian church is the recipient setting.
The day of the Lord and Christ's coming shape the letter.
Judgment language comforts the afflicted and warns the rebellious.
Perseverance under pressure is a major concern.
